subject: Geography
central_question: How have geological history and geomorphic processes produced India’s major structural and physiographic divisions?
in_scope_units: Geological history and the three broad geological divisions of India.
The Peninsular Block, Himalayas and Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain.
The concept of physiography and India’s six major divisions.
The Northern and Northeastern Mountains and Northern Plain.
The Peninsular Plateau and its subdivisions.
The Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and island groups.
banned_topics: Detailed river-basin descriptions, which belong to Drainage System.
Detailed monsoon mechanisms, which belong to Climate.
Earth’s internal layers and seismic waves, which belong to Interior of the Earth.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Himalayas and Peninsular Block have the same geological character.
known_pitfalls.correction: The Peninsular Block is ancient, rigid and stable; the Himalayas are young, weak and flexible.
Streams may disappear in coarse Bhabar deposits and re-emerge in marshy Tarai.

known_pitfalls.claim: The two coastal plains have the same origin and width.
known_pitfalls.correction: The western plain is narrow and submerged; the eastern plain is broader and emergent.
Lakshadweep is built of coral deposits; only some Bay of Bengal islands are volcanic.

known_pitfalls.claim: The Eastern Ghats form an unbroken wall.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are discontinuous and deeply cut by rivers.

recommended_example_progression: Use Exercise 2(ii) to identify India’s cold desert.
Use Exercise 2(iii) to explain why the western coastal plain lacks deltas.
Use Exercise 3(i) to compare the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal island groups.
Use Exercise 3(iii) to trace geomorphological features from Badrinath to the Sunderbans.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Exercises 1(i–ii), 2(i–iii), 3(i–iii), and a two-part Project/Activity.
